name: repeatedly solve with a shifted matrix to amplify the eigenvector nearest the shift
mechanism: instead of multiplying by the matrix, solve a linear system with the matrix minus a chosen shift each round; the eigenvalue closest to the shift becomes the dominant one of the inverse, so the vector converges to its eigenvector

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Inverse iteration' in section Computational mathematics / Numerical algorithms / Linear algebra:

requires: a shift near the wanted eigenvalue (policy)
fails_when: each round costs a solve; a shift exactly on an eigenvalue is singular
